## **Survey Participation and Extension**

The team decided to extend the survey by one week to boost participation without delaying feedback turnaround. (02:01)  
- The survey has collected **422 responses** over the first **12 days** since launch on March 18th.  
- Carol Meichner-Smith approved extending the survey until **April 8th at midnight** to allow more time for responses.  
- Karthik Rao confirmed the extension was applied directly in the platform with no technical issues.  
- The extension aims to increase participation while still enabling timely analysis and reporting.  

Karthik and Carol reviewed participation data by club location and departments to target promotion efforts. (04:00)  
- Karthik will provide detailed data showing participation counts by **location and department**, including total team sizes.  
- This data will help Carol and Elena identify units with low participation to focus outreach.  
- Elena maintains a leaderboard by location to track progress, which supports motivating clubs.  
- The data includes all teams regardless of anonymity thresholds to ensure full visibility.  

## **Reminder Strategy and Engagement Boost**

Reminder messages have driven most survey responses, leading to a planned schedule of follow-up communications. (07:30)  
- Initial daily responses reached about **50+ submissions per day** after launch, with peaks near **59 submissions** on days reminders were sent.  
- Reminders through email, WhatsApp, and SMS accounted for **200 to 300 submissions** out of total responses so far.  
- Recent days with no reminders saw a drop to under **15 submissions** per day.  
- Karthik and Carol agreed on sending a **WhatsApp reminder on April 2nd** (Friday) and a **final email reminder on April 7th** (Tuesday).  

The team decided to reduce SMS reminders due to lower engagement compared to email and WhatsApp. (10:30)  
- Carol noted SMS had less impact on participation relative to other channels.  
- Karthik recommended using WhatsApp first on Friday, followed by email on Tuesday to maximize reach.  
- The chosen channels align with observed response patterns and help avoid overloading participants.  
- This staggered approach aims to capture last-minute respondents before survey closure.  

## **On-Site Promotion and Survey Accessibility**

Carol and Karthik discussed encouraging clubs to hold short internal meetings to increase survey response rates. (11:30)  
- Elena has already created a QR code flyer for clubs to share, which Karthik will resend for updated distribution.  
- Carol suggested clubs could organize **5 to 10 minute sessions** where employees scan the QR code and complete the survey on the spot.  
- This approach targets operational staff who may not regularly check email or SMS.  
- Karthik emphasized this as a best practice seen in other companies to improve participation among frontline workers.  

The use of QR codes and brief club meetings is a low-cost, practical way to boost survey visibility. (12:30)  
- Clubs can print flyers with QR codes to display in common areas or meeting rooms.  
- Internal meetings create dedicated time for employees to engage without distractions.  
- This method reduces reliance on digital reminders alone and addresses accessibility gaps.  
- Carol will coordinate with club leaders to implement this during the extended survey period.  

## **Reporting Preparation and Coordination**

Carol requested a meeting to finalize reporting requirements before survey closure to enable smooth report generation. (14:30)  
- Karthik agreed to schedule a session this week to review the desired report formats and content with Carol, Elena, and Christie.  
- The goal is to clarify expectations so the people science team can prepare reports immediately after survey ends.  
- Carol prefers a **45-minute meeting**, aiming to finish sooner if possible, with tentative timing set for **Thursday at 9:30 AM Eastern**.  
- Karthik will send invitations and ensure alignment on reporting deliverables and timelines.  

This planning ensures quick turnaround on actionable insights once survey data collection ends. (16:00)  
- Early coordination helps prevent delays in feedback reporting and decision-making.  
- Carol expressed trust in Karthik’s team to handle the reporting if she cannot attend.  
- Karthik will follow up with requested data and provide ongoing support to address questions.  
- The meeting will confirm final report structure and set deadlines for delivery after April 8th.

- **Data Cleanup Prioritized:** Focus on fixing duplicates and hierarchy mapping for accurate employee reporting and survey results.  
- **Survey Refresh Post-Cleanup:** Updated data will allow for accurate manager-employee reporting in upcoming surveys.  
- **Email Format Standardization:** Automation will normalize email cases to prevent future duplication issues.  
- **Unique Identifier Improvements:** Discussed using user IDs as alternatives to emails for unique records.  
- **Regular Data Quality Checks:** Quarterly reviews by HR admins recommended to maintain data integrity and catch anomalies.  
- **Documentation for HR Admins:** Creating clear instructions aims to empower admins and reduce manual support requests.

## **Employee Data Accuracy and Cleanup**

The team agreed on a thorough cleanup of employee data to fix duplicates and hierarchy mapping issues for accurate reporting and survey results.

- **Cleaning duplicates and fixing hierarchy mapping is prioritized for data accuracy** (02:05)  
    - The issue stems from emails with case differences creating duplicate employee profiles.  
    - Yugi explained duplicates caused incorrect manager-reportee relationships and reporting errors.  
    - The engineering team prepared a list of duplicate profiles for Sean's team to review and confirm which records to keep or deactivate.  
    - Once confirmed, duplicates will be deactivated, and manager mappings corrected to reflect the true org structure.

- **Fixing data will enable a survey refresh with accurate reporting** (07:02)  
    - Yugi confirmed survey data will be refreshed after data cleanup to reflect correct manager-employee links.  
    - This will resolve current discrepancies in survey results caused by scattered mappings.  
    - Sean emphasized the importance of reviewing refreshed survey results to validate accuracy.

- **Sean's team will enforce consistent email formatting to prevent future duplicates** (07:45)  
    - Sean committed to normalizing email case in their automation using SQL logic to lowercase all emails.  
    - This step aims to prevent case-related duplicates going forward.  
    - Sean will send an updated cleaned file quickly to enable the fix to start promptly.  
    - Karthik and Yugi stressed receiving the corrected file soon for a timely weekend fix.

- **One-time bulk fix expected to complete by Monday with ongoing processes to prevent recurrence** (14:38)  
    - Karthik estimated a couple of days to validate and fix data internally after receiving the clean file.  
    - Future uploads will include duplicate checks and confirmation notifications after sync.  
    - This will improve transparency on file processing status for Sean’s team.  
    - Sean offered to support day or night for quick resolution and automation improvements.

## **Technical Validation and Automation Enhancement**

The team focused on improving automation and validation processes to ensure clean data feeds and reduce manual fixes.

- **Automation will include SQL logic to standardize emails and prevent duplicates** (13:15)  
    - Sean plans to implement SQL to lowercase emails and format names consistently before sending files.  
    - This reduces manual cleanup and errors from inconsistent email entries.  
    - Collaboration between Sean and Disha will finalize this automation step quickly.  
    - This approach aligns with the platform’s requirement for consistent unique identifiers.

- **Current unique identifier challenges addressed with potential alternatives** (09:29)  
    - Karthik explained the system uses email as the unique identifier due to lack of alternatives.  
    - Sean pointed out the data does include a user ID field that could serve as a unique key.  
    - The team discussed reusing emails for rehires and the challenge of tracking inactive/reactivated profiles.  
    - They plan to include this logic in future validations to avoid conflicts.

- **Regular data quality checks recommended to maintain integrity** (10:49)  
    - Sean suggested quarterly or biannual manual reviews by HR admins to catch anomalies early.  
    - He plans to create simple checklists and guides for his HR team to monitor data health.  
    - Karthik supported this approach as a good complement to automated validations.

- **Transparent Pricing Structure:** Annual subscription for 2,000 employees is $35,000, with no hidden fees and a quick five-week implementation timeline.

## **Product Offering and Integration**

The meeting established CultureMonkey as a flexible, employee engagement platform designed to replace costly vendors like Qualtrics and Culture Amp with a strong healthcare sector footprint (02:28).

- **Comprehensive Data Migration and Customization** (01:28)  
    - CultureMonkey supports migrating historic data or raw data downloads from previous platforms.  
    - The platform allows importing existing frameworks, questions, and templates or using CultureMonkey’s own customizable repositories.  
    - A dedicated people science team customizes surveys specific to the client’s needs for deeper insights.  
    - Ashley was advised to check if historic data from Qualtrics is available for migration.

- **Seamless HR System Integration and Survey Delivery** (04:54)  
    - Integration with Sage HRMS ensures automatic employee data syncing for up-to-date survey distribution.  
    - Surveys can be delivered via multiple channels including email, text, WhatsApp, Microsoft Teams, Slack, QR codes, and kiosks.  
    - The platform supports continuous listening with automated lifecycle surveys covering onboarding, exit, and milestone events.  
    - Multilingual support covers 130 languages, with current usage planned in English for North American employees.

- **Real-Time Reporting and Leadership Consumption** (06:13)  
    - CultureMonkey provides instant dashboards and creates custom reports in leadership-preferred formats like PowerPoint and PDFs.  
    - Custom reports, including benchmarking and design language preferences, are included in the subscription with no extra cost.  
    - An in-house AI chatbot assists HR leaders and managers with analytics, comparisons, and action recommendations post-survey.

- **Manager Dashboards and Anonymity Thresholds** (19:57)  
    - Managers with more than five direct reports receive dashboards; threshold can be lowered to three if needed.  
    - Managers see overall engagement, NPS, participation, and driver themes but not individual feedback to maintain privacy.  
    - HR leaders can impersonate managers’ views for oversight and support.

## **Survey Design and Participation Tracking**

CultureMonkey delivers a highly modular and customizable survey system with advanced tracking and real-time analytics for engagement improvement (09:14).

- **Flexible Survey Templates and Modes** (09:14)  
    - Pre-built templates cover topics like retention, inclusivity, and leadership, with options to customize or create exclusive surveys.  
    - Surveys can be anonymous or non-anonymous, with the ability to create QR code-only surveys for on-the-go feedback or whistleblowing.  
    - Dynamic questions allow different question sets for different teams within the same survey.

- **Multi-Channel Reminder Configuration and Live Participation Tracking** (10:25)  
    - Survey reminders can be configured across different channels and days to optimize response rates.  
    - A live participation tracker monitors employee responses in real time, highlighting preferred communication channels and engagement levels.

- **Heat Map Visualization and Demographic Drill-Down** (11:35)
